content:
Allison Grant: Hey folks, tuning pass on SLOs + alert thresholds for Usage Insights APIs + export jobs before we open the beta wider. Want to make sure we’re not paging ourselves to death but also catch real issues.

Allison Grant: Draft dashboards here (staging data right now):
- API: https://grafana.redwoodinfra.net/d/usage-insights-api/usage-insights-api-health?orgId=1
- Exports: https://grafana.redwoodinfra.net/d/usage-insights-export/usage-insights-export-jobs?orgId=1
- Pipeline lag: https://grafana.redwoodinfra.net/d/usage-insights-pipeline/usage-insights-pipeline-lag?orgId=1

Logan Wright: +1. We have some noisy spikes on the query side when cache is cold / after deploy. Would prefer warning alerts on latency until we have the cache warmup in place.

Nadia Rahman: For freshness/lag: metering events arrive late sometimes (esp. Dedicated w/ batching). We need to distinguish “pipeline down” from “expected late arrivals”.

Allison Grant: Yup. Proposing SLOs:
- Insights APIs availability: 99.9% (rolling 30d)
- Insights APIs latency: p95 < 600ms for `GET /v1/insights/routes` and < 800ms for `GET /v1/insights/routes/:id` (rolling 5m window for alerting, SLO measured daily)
- Export job success rate: 99.5% (30d) + separate SLO for “completed within 10m” at 99%
- Freshness: “data delay” p95 < 15m (hosted), p95 < 30m (dedicated) (measured as aggregate watermark - event_time)

Caleb Johnson: Latency numbers seem high for the route list endpoint? Product asked for “snappy table experience”. But maybe ok for initial beta if we cache.

Chloe Martin: The console is going to call route list on filter changes + pagination. If we let p95 drift to 600ms we’ll feel it. Can we set SLO at 400ms and alert at 800ms?

Logan Wright: The query cost limiter is already in (max partitions per query), but we’re still seeing ~450-700ms when cardinality is high (lots of routes) unless cache hits.

Thomas Baird: Cardinality is the driver here. If an org has 50k routes (bad tagging), the query has to hit more groups even with limits. We should alert on cardinality separately, not punish latency SLO for it.

Allison Grant: Agree. We can do:
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 400ms (route list), p95 < 600ms (route detail)
- Alert thresholds higher to avoid paging during expected spikes
- Add a separate warning alert for “route cardinality budget exceeded” per org/project

Nadia Rahman: On freshness: I’m nervous about paging on “data delay” alone because late events (replays, delayed token metering) can look like lag. Can we page on “watermark not advancing” + “ingest volume drop” instead?

Allison Grant: Yes. I’d like two signals:
1) Watermark not advancing (hard) = page
2) Watermark p95 delay > threshold (soft) = warning

Kevin Osei: For exports: we should definitely page on audit log write failures? If export completes but audit event fails, that’s a compliance problem.

Allison Grant: Good call. Separate alert:
- `audit_log_write_errors` rate > 0 for exports = page (low volume, should be clean)

Grafana Bot: Alert rule suggestion imported: usage-insights-api-5xx-burnrate (multiwindow) [created by Allison Grant]

Caleb Johnson: For API burn rate, can we do the standard 2% / 5% budget burn rules? (e.g. 14x over 5m, 6x over 30m). Otherwise we’ll flap.

Allison Grant: Yep, default burn-rate pair:
- Page: 14x over 5m AND 6x over 30m
- Ticket: 3x over 2h AND 1x over 6h
applies to 5xx availability SLO.

Chloe Martin: What do we count as “bad” for export job completion? Some exports are legitimately big (close to max rows). We need a cap.

Logan Wright: Export guardrails in PR: max time range 31d, max rows 200k, hard timeout 12m. So SLO “completed within 10m” seems reasonable.

Allison Grant: Ok alerting proposal for exports:
- Page: `export_jobs_failed / export_jobs_created` > 2% over 15m (and > N=20 jobs) OR queue backlog > 200 for 10m
- Ticket: p95 export runtime > 8m over 2h
- Page: `export_jobs_timeout` > 1% over 15m (and > N=20)
- Page: audit log write errors > 0 over 5m

Nadia Rahman: For pipeline lag/backfill: during backfill we’ll intentionally run recompute and watermark might jump. Can we auto-silence during backfill window? Or at least a label to exclude.

Thomas Baird: We can set a `recompute_job_active=1` metric from the backfill tooling. Then alert expression can be `unless recompute_job_active`.

Allison Grant: Perfect. Please add that metric if it’s not already in.

Logan Wright: It’s in my branch but not merged. I’ll land it today.

Talia Benson: Can we capture decisions + owners here so I can update the GA gating checklist? We keep getting asked “what has to be green”.

Allison Grant: Sure.
Decisions (proposed):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% (insights APIs)
- Latency SLO targets: route list p95 < 400ms; route detail p95 < 600ms
- Alerting: multi-window burn rate for 5xx; latency alerts start as warning (ticket) until beta stabilizes
- Freshness: page on “watermark not advancing” + ingest volume drop; warn on p95 delay thresholds; suppress while `recompute_job_active=1`
- Exports: page on failure/timeout rates w/ min volume; page on backlog; page on audit log write errors

Allison Grant: Owners:
- Logan: recompute_job_active metric + confirm export runtime metrics emitted
- Nadia: define “watermark not advancing” detection logic (what window) + expected late arrival notes
- Chloe: confirm console perf expectations / whether we need stricter latency gate for GA
- Allison: implement alert rules + route cardinality warning alert

Caleb Johnson: For “watermark not advancing”, suggest: if watermark delta < 60s over 10m AND ingest rate > 0 (or should be > 0) then page. Need to avoid paging overnight low traffic.

Nadia Rahman: +1. We can key off “expected traffic” by checking metering events count for same hour last week? Might be overkill.

Allison Grant: Let’s keep it simple for beta:
- Page when watermark flat for 15m AND ingest events > 100 in that window (so we only page when there’s real traffic)
We can refine once we have baseline.

Kevin Osei: Re audit events: also want a dashboard panel showing export audit events per hour vs export jobs created. Helps spot partial failures.

Allison Grant: Added as TODO in the exports dashboard. Kevin, if you have the event name + labels from the spec, drop it here.

Kevin Osei: Event is `usage_report.export.created` and `usage_report.export.downloaded`. Labels: `actor_user_id`, `org_id`, `project_id`, `filters_hash`, `format`, `time_range`, `export_job_id`. For dashboard we can just count by org_id/project_id.

Allison Grant: Great.

Chloe Martin: One more: do we need an alert for query cost limiter trips? If we’re returning 400 w/ “query too expensive”, console will show errors.

Logan Wright: Yes, we emit `insights_query_rejected_total{reason="cost_limit"}`. Should ticket on sustained > 0.1% of requests.

Allison Grant: Added: ticket alert when cost_limit rejects > 0.5% over 30m (min N=200). Paging only if it’s > 5%.

Talia Benson: Thanks all. I’ll paste the decisions into the rollout checklist + link these dashboards.

Allison Grant: Cool. I’ll wire the rules up today in observability-pack and post screenshots once it’s in staging.

Grafana Bot: Dashboard updated: usage-insights-export-jobs (revision 12) by Allison Grant
